The patch simplifies the boundary checks in find_va_links() of vmalloc.c by removing redundant comparisons, relying on the invariant that both vmap_areas have start ≤ end, resulting in fewer conditionals and cleaner code.
Adds a central definition for the 'linux,input-type' property in the input devicetree binding and updates existing bindings to use it, removing duplicated definitions and descriptions.
Changes the return type of sparx5_mact_find from bool to int in both implementation and header to reflect that the function returns error codes, correcting a type mismatch.
Corrects a spelling mistake in a comment of the protection_keys selftest; no functional code change.
Replace call_rcu with call_rcu_hurry in rcu_sync to avoid slowdown introduced by power‑saving changes to call_rcu, restoring original behavior.
Adds entries for new Qualcomm SoCs and PMIC models to the socinfo driver by extending static lookup tables.
Replace the multiline macro vt6655_mac_word_reg_bits_on with an equivalent function, adding its definition in mac.c and declaration in mac.h, to satisfy checkpatch style rules.
The patch replaces manual Tx queue pointer updates in omap_8250_dma_tx_complete with a call to uart_xmit_advance, aligning the driver with the generic UART API for better consistency and robustness.

The patch removes dead code in the device‑mapper driver: deletes the unused bio_setup_sector helper, eliminates bio_advance calls, and directly sets bio size fields, because earlier changes eliminated the need for looping over bios.
Adds support in perf to record the guest CPU for hypervisor (QEMU) threads by extending the thread structure with a guest_cpu field and setting it when processing id_index events.
Adds the P1 Gen 3 (LEN040f) identifier to the Synaptics driver so that the InterTouch (rmi4) touchpad is enabled on ThinkPad P1 G3, allowing the driver to recognize and initialize the device.

Adds a hardware workaround Wa_16013835468 for Intel display pipelines, introducing a helper to select register bits per pipe, adjusting PSR enable code to set/clear the bit based on vblank timing, and updating register definitions.
The commit adds the const qualifier to many static initialization tables and to function parameters/struct fields that reference them, making the data read‑only and updating signatures accordingly.
Updates the mt8195 pinctrl device-tree binding YAML to allow subnodes within pinctrl groups, adds schema refinements and examples showing multiple pin configuration nodes.

The commit adds a runtime check for the presence of Xilinx ZynqMP SHA3 hardware via firmware API, updates Kconfig to depend on ZYNQMP_FIRMWARE, and simplifies driver registration with module_platform_driver, preventing the driver from loading on unsupported platforms.

Adds a version field to the EDIF BSG interface, updates code to verify this version, removes unused fields and adjusts struct sizes, refactoring the driver to clean up and prepare for future extensions.
The commit corrects a misspelled word in a comment within include/rdma/opa_vnic.h, changing 'structrue' to 'structure' without altering any code logic.
Adds Device Tree bindings and a header file for the Qualcomm SM6350 camera clock controller, defining compatible string, properties, and clock identifiers.

The patch modifies rtl8xxxu_print_chipinfo to compute the chip cut character directly (using 'A' + chip_cut for values 0‑15) and removes the previous switch that printed "unknown" for cuts beyond E, improving the logging of chip version.

The patch separates the handling of HK_FLAG_WQ and HK_FLAG_DOMAIN when obtaining the housekeeping cpumask, replacing a combined flag call with two distinct calls and an AND, to allow independent manipulation of each cpumask for future cpuset support.
The commit updates the email address of John Garry in the MAINTAINERS file for the arm64 perf tooling section.
Removes the .owner field from the Sunplus Ethernet platform driver struct because the core sets it automatically, silencing a Coccinelle warning.

Adds power‑management support to the Microchip PCI1XXXX SPI driver by implementing suspend and resume callbacks, storing hardware configuration before suspend and restoring it on resume, and registering the PM ops in the PCI driver structure.
The commit adjusts the baud‑rate handling in ftdi_sio.c, replacing a post‑switch check with a default case to correctly support the historic 300 bps rate that was mistakenly mapped to 9600 bps.
Adds handling of PERF_SAMPLE_DATA_SRC in AMD IBS perf events by converting IBS raw fields into perf_mem_data_src structures, exposing detailed memory operation information to perf tools.
The commit adds a vfree() call for the memory allocated by vzmalloc() when ice_read_flash_module() fails, preventing a leak in ice_get_orom_civd_data().
Adds self‑test cases for BPF that verify passing read‑only memory to global functions is rejected, introduces a new test program, and adjusts test harness to exercise two handlers.

The commit adds a standard sysfs "label" attribute for ChromeOS EC sensors based on known locations, removes the custom "location" attribute and the loc field from core structures, and updates drivers to use the new label.
Updates the fsl,clk-source property in the LX2160A device tree to use the required '/bits/ 8 <0>' syntax, fixing a warning about property length.
Adds Roman Gushchin as a co-maintainer for the memory controller subsystem by inserting a line in the MAINTAINERS file.

Replaces iscsi_create_conn with iscsi_alloc_conn and adds the connection to sysfs only after dd_data is initialized, removing the unused create function. This stops a NULL‑pointer dereference when userspace accesses connection attributes.
The patch changes the cast of of_device_get_match_data(&pdev->dev) from (enum mxcmci_type) to (uintptr_t) to silence a clang warning about casting a void pointer to a smaller integer type.
The patch adds the missing bitrate_const check to can_changelink(), allowing CAN devices with fixed bit rates to be configured via netlink without a dummy do_set_bittiming callback.

The patch adds cleanup of the stream context array on allocation failure in xhci_alloc_stream_info(), preventing a memory leak by calling xhci_free_stream_ctx() before freeing the stream info structure.
Adds NULL checks after ioremap calls for SRAM, rmem, and amem in the ray_cs driver; on failure it jumps to the existing error handling to avoid later NULL dereference.

The patch changes vsock_connect to use mod_delayed_work instead of schedule_delayed_work and adds a sock_put when the work was already pending, correcting an unbalanced sock_hold that caused a memory leak reported by syzbot.
The commit replaces the legacy i2c-at91 text binding with a new Device Tree JSON‑schema YAML file, adding structured validation and modern documentation while removing the old .txt file.
Adds a macro for the LCOUNT mask in sdw_intel.h and replaces inline GENMASK(2,0) uses with this macro in driver code, improving readability.

The patch updates the habanalabs driver’s map_block function to initialize output parameters, call get_hw_block_id, and only set the handle when that call succeeds, returning an error otherwise, thus preventing a spurious valid handle from being returned.
Fixes the WARN_ON condition in ice_vsi_rebuild to correctly detect a missing VF pointer for VF-type VSIs, preventing a kernel warning and error during VF reset.
Removes dead fallback DMA‑32 mask code from hisi_sas driver, because a 64‑bit mask never fails when dma_mask is set, simplifying the driver.

Adds a call to set_counter_value in the armada_37xx_wdt_set_timeout function so that the hardware watchdog counter used for timeout is updated when the WDIOC_SETTIMEOUT ioctl is invoked, correcting the previous omission.

Removes the redundant is_enabled field and its associated enable/disable/is_enabled functions from the ux500 PRCMU clock driver, relying on the core's existing enable count, and updates clk_ops tables accordingly.

The patch reorganizes XIP‑related conditional code in arch/riscv/mm/init.c, moving extern declarations and macro definitions, grouping them to minimise #ifdef CONFIG_XIP_KERNEL usage, without altering runtime behaviour.

The patch introduces a device counter and mutex to allow changing the target driver database root directory only when no SCSI target devices are registered, fixing the previous overly strict restriction.

Adds error‑handling to libbpf's legacy kprobe attachment: if determining the perf type or opening the perf event fails, the previously created kprobe_event is removed, avoiding stale events and -EBUSY errors.

Adds Mediatek mt8186 SCP support to the remoteproc driver by defining new registers, implementing a before_load routine, providing of_data for mt8186, and registering the compatible string in the device match table.

The patch refactors the speakup_dummy driver to use an indexed var_t array and adds module parameters exposing each driver variable’s default value, allowing these defaults to be set at module load time.
Adds a deprecated "riscv,clint0" compatible string to the sifive,clint devicetree binding to stop dt-validate errors with QEMU-generated DTBs.

The patch modifies swiotlb_max_mapping_size() to subtract the rounded‑up minimum alignment mask, ensuring the reported maximum DMA mapping size respects the alignment constraints. This corrects a boot‑time failure on Hyper‑V where the previous calculation allowed an impossible buffer size.

The patch replaces the legacy command‑buffer manager with the unified memory manager, removing cb_mgr structures and updating all CB handling code to use hl_cb_get via the mem_mgr, effectively a large refactor of the CB flow.

The patch changes vmbus_request_addr to return VMBUS_RQST_ERROR when the transaction ID is zero, preventing a NULL dereference in netvsc_send_completion, and updates comments about ID 0 being reserved for Hyper-V.
Adds fields to source buffer and a helper to detect and apply JPEG resolution changes, moving the previous inline logic into a dedicated function to support dynamic source changes.
Replace memcpy with copy_map_value in bpf_selem_alloc to avoid overwriting the spin‑lock field in map values, ensuring correct initialization of the lock.

Caches the remote address early and uses the cached copy when announcing it, preventing the remote address from being overwritten after the PM lock is released during processing of consecutive ADD_ADDR options.
The commit separates Zynq A05 DDR controller support from the Synopsys DW uMCTL2 DDRC binding by updating the existing YAML schema, adding a new Zynq‑A05 binding file, and adjusting MAINTAINERS.
Removes the 'status = "okay"' line from the i2s1 node in the Rock Pi 4 device tree, keeping the I2S1 controller disabled so the pins can function as GPIO, matching the hardware's default behavior.
The commit adds definitions for ADC clock and reset lines in the Renesas r9a07g043 CPG driver, extending the driver to support the ADC hardware block.
The patch deletes the declaration and assignment of the variable 'mdss' in msm_drv.c because the code that used it was removed, eliminating a clang -Wunused-but-set-variable warning.
Adds new skb drop reason enums and trace mappings, and modifies tcp_v4_rcv to set a drop_reason and call kfree_skb_reason, enabling detailed logging of why a packet is dropped.

The patch deletes an obsolete comment and a negative‑value check in highmem_dirtyable_memory() because a previous commit guarantees the variable cannot be negative or overflow. It results in no functional change, only code cleanup.

Updates the MAINTAINERS entry for the Mediatek JPEG driver to point to the new yaml bindings and broadens the pattern to include both decoder and encoder files, fixing a broken reference used by get_maintainer.pl.

The commit refactors the xfs_buf_incore API to return an error code and place the buffer in an out‑parameter, adds the XBF_INCORE flag, removes the old function, and updates all callers to use the new signature, aligning it with other buffer APIs.
Fixes a DSC slice calculation bug where resetting min_slices_h to 0 could incorrectly keep DSC enabled even when max slice cannot fit the pixel clock, by reordering the is_dsc_possible check.
Adds clock and reset definitions for PWM channels 8‑14 in the Renesas R9A09G011 CPG driver and marks the CPERI_GRPF_PCLK as critical, enabling Linux to manage those PWM clocks.

Corrects MTU handling in the LAN966x driver by reading the hardware MTU, adding missing header/FCS and skb_shared_info space, and fixing the rollback write, preventing FDMA allocation failures when MTU changes.
Adds per‑CPU structures and functions to record hypervisor stack base, overflow stack, frame pointer and PC for non‑protected nVHE, enabling the host to unwind the hypervisor backtrace from EL1.
The patch corrects a typo in an error log string within the ASoC mchp-spdifrx driver, changing "PMC" to "PCM".

The commit sets the fb_modifiers_not_supported flag in the amdgpu virtual KMS driver, indicating that framebuffer modifiers are unsupported, which stops GDM3 from failing to set a mode on virtual displays.
The commit corrects a Chinese translation of the devicetree usage-model documentation, ensuring the term "machine_desc" remains untranslated to avoid a half‑translated word.
Adds internal helper functions to read a block register and to verify its presence, enabling safe checking of block registers when PEC is used.
Replaces the multiline macro vt6655_mac_word_reg_bits_off with a regular function, adding its definition in mac.c and declaration in mac.h to satisfy checkpatch.
Adjusts the sysfs-fs-erofs ABI documentation to eliminate Sphinx indentation and block‑quote warnings by adding a missing colon, a blank line, and fixing list indentation.

The patch adds support for BA CAM version 1 chips (e.g., 8852c) by extending chip info, adjusting the H2C BA CAM command to use the correct fields, and initializing additional dynamic BA CAM entries during driver start. It also updates chip descriptors for 8852a/8852c.
The patch only adjusts whitespace/indentation in dcn32_hwseq.c to fix a smatch warning, without altering any logic or functionality.

Adds independent TX/RX FIFO flush bits for newer JZ SoCs, introduces a flag to distinguish shared vs independent flush behavior, and updates startup logic to flush the correct FIFO, fixing missing RX flush on those SoCs.
Enables QUP and GPI DMA nodes in the sm6350 device tree by setting their status to "okay", allowing I2C peripherals to be functional on the Sony Xperia Lena platform.
Adds PCI device IDs for Intel Raptor Lake PCH‑S to the intel‑lpss driver, enabling the driver to recognize and bind to these new LPSS devices.
The commit removes a duplicated word in a comment within drivers/crypto/n2_core.c, changing 'to to' to 'to' without altering any code logic.
Adds the USB ID of Accuphase DAC-60 option card to the DSD format quirk switch, enabling native DSD up to DSD256 for that device when the correct altsetting is selected.
Adds support for the VCN 4.0 IP block, including firmware handling, register definitions, initialization, power/clock gating, ring management, and interrupt handling.

The patch adds EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL statements for six decoder power-management functions in the MediaTek VCodec driver, enabling other kernel modules to reference them when the decoder is built as a loadable module.
The patch adds READ_ONCE() around all reads of sysctl_igmp_qrv in IGMP and AMT code to eliminate data races caused by concurrent modifications of this sysctl variable.
Adds a local boolean rx_timeout to the IRQ handler to make the timeout check clearer; no functional change, only code readability improvement.

The patch adds proper error handling for nvmem_device_find in the PTP OCP driver: it checks for IS_ERR pointers before using them, returns the error code, and avoids calling nvmem_device_put on error pointers.

The commit renames the ID_AA64MMFR2_EL1.VARange field from the historic LVA identifier to VARange across assembler macros, sysreg definitions, CPU feature tables, and early boot code, aligning kernel naming with the ARM DDI0487H.a specification without altering functionality.
The patch updates comments in rzg2l_thermal.c: replaces an unclear comment with a clearer one, fixes a typo (caliberation → calibration), and adjusts comment formatting to match kernel coding style.
Removes a duplicated 'the' in a comment within vas.c, fixing a typo in the code documentation.
The patch deletes the unused local variable `cnt` in `recv_func` of the r8188eu driver, simplifying the loop that processes pending frames. No functional change, only removal of dead code.

The patch changes igc_release_swfw_sync_i225 to stop spinning on a hardware semaphore. If the semaphore cannot be obtained (e.g., hardware surprise‑removed), it now logs an error and returns instead of looping forever.

Moves maybe_wait_bpf_programs() out of the per‑element loop in generic_map_delete_batch, so the RCU barrier runs only once after all deletions, reducing unnecessary synchronization before returning to userspace.

Refactors KVM selftest state_test to eliminate hard‑coded VCPU_ID, using vm_create_with_one_vcpu()/vm_recreate_with_one_vcpu() and passing a struct kvm_vcpu pointer; also switches to vcpu_run(). No kernel code change.

The patch removes CONFIG_PM_SLEEP #ifdef guards around suspend/resume functions, replaces SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS with DEFINE_SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS, and sets the driver .pm field via pm_sleep_ptr(). This lets the compiler drop the PM code when sleep support is disabled, simplifying the driver and reducing guard‑related errors.
The commit updates the header of tools/testing/radix-tree/maple.c, changing the file description line and extending the copyright notice to cover 2018-2022 and adding an author line.
Converts the rc5t583 I2C driver probe to use the .probe_new callback, removing the unused i2c_device_id argument and aligning with the newer I2C driver API.

The patch refactors vchiq_get_state to check g_state.remote and its initialization separately, returning NULL early and simplifying the final return, improving code readability without changing external behavior.

Moves the efi32_pe_entry assembly routine from the __HEAD section to the .text section, adjusting relative address calculations so it can later be compiled as a separate unit. No functional behavior change, only code organization.
Moves two constant arrays defining CEC register headers/lengths from adv7511.h to adv7511_cec.c because they are only used there, eliminating unused‑variable warnings when the CEC config is disabled.
Adds CLK_OPS_PARENT_ENABLE flag to pixel and byte clock sources in the SM6350 driver so the parent clock is enabled during set_rate, fixing failures where set_rate could not succeed.
Renames driver variables and logic to use the newer ASoC DAI clock provider/consumer terminology, updating format masks and error messages accordingly, without altering functionality.

Adds a boolean flag to gsi_channel_data_valid and runtime checks that ensure a command channel is TX, its TLV count fits the FIFO size, and TRE limits are respected, preventing misconfiguration of IPA command channels.

The patch corrects the layout of struct result_data_desc by removing mixed non‑bit‑field members and converting them to u32 bit‑fields, eliminating unwanted padding that affected zero‑ing and configuration calculations.

Adds vcap_entry_get calls before moving VCAP filter entries so that hardware hit counters are read back and not overwritten with stale values during filter reordering, correcting inaccurate statistics.
The patch deletes a conditional definition of IS_SWAPFILE in fs/nfs/file.c because the macro is already always defined elsewhere, making the code dead and unnecessary.

The patch corrects tps65219_set_bypass to use the regulator's is_enabled() callback instead of checking the presence of the enable operation, ensuring proper detection of an enabled regulator, and removes an unused ret variable.

Adds a completed_id field to the IPA GSI transaction info structure and updates the transaction handling code to advance and verify this ID, removing temporary WARN checks that were only there for debugging.
The patch deletes the now‑unused tstamp pointer from struct mlx5e_txqsq and removes the corresponding assignments in the driver, cleaning up dead code introduced after a prior PTP migration.
The patch updates the NXP NCI I2C driver to detect i2c_master_recv errors (negative return) and exit without printing a misleading "Invalid frame length" error, returning the error code directly.
Adds devicetree binding entries qcom,smem-states and qcom,smem-state-names to the ath11k documentation to enable Wake‑on‑Wireless support for the WCN6750 chipset.
Introduces AGGREGATOR_MAX_GPIOS=512 and replaces ARCH_NR_GPIOS in bitmap allocation, parsing and iteration, limiting the bitmap size used by the gpio-aggregator driver.
Reformats comment blocks in the r8188eu driver to follow the drivers/net coding style, without altering code behavior.

Adds a new device‑tree binding YAML file for the Renesas RZ/G2L (IA55) interrupt controller, defining compatible strings, required properties, and an example node, thereby enabling kernel support for this hardware.
Changes PS_RDY_CHECK return type from u8 to bool, matching its true/false semantics; updates the function signature in the r8188eu driver.
Adds a guard in gfs2_glock_dq() to verify the holder is still queued before dequeuing, preventing a race where an async lock request that already failed is dequeued again.
The patch removes the driver‑specific yesno() helper, adds <linux/string_helpers.h>, and replaces all its calls with the generic str_yes_no() function, cleaning up the code.

The commit removes an out-of-bounds array write in imx-jpeg driver error handling. When parsing fails, the slot index may be the default MXC_MAX_SLOTS, causing jpeg->slot_data[ctx->slot] access beyond the array, corrupting num_domains and leading to kernel panic on reload. Deleting the write fixes this.
Adds two new compatible strings for DH electronics i.MX8M Plus DHCOM SoM and PDK2 board to the arm/fsl.yaml DT binding document, updating documentation to reflect supported hardware.

The commit corrects translate_desc() in the vhost driver by storing the original end address (last) before the loop and using it unchanged in each vhost_iotlb_itree_first() call, fixing incorrect range handling.
Adds a guard `i > 0` before accessing `args[i-1]` in next_arg, preventing out‑of‑bounds read that caused a kernel page fault when parsing a quoted argument at the start of the command line.

Reorders functions and static symbols in the via686a hardware monitoring driver to eliminate unnecessary forward declarations, improving code layout and avoiding cyclic dependencies without altering runtime behavior.

The patch modifies acpi_processor_get_platform_limit() to skip QoS updates when the _PPC value hasn't changed and adds safety checks; it also resets the stored limit during init and uses a default QoS value for consistency.
The commit deletes the arm64 head.o entry from scripts/head-object-list.txt, removing unnecessary special link ordering because the linker script already ensures the required .head.text is first.

The patch moves RAS‑DES register definitions to the common header and changes the Tegra194 driver to discover the RAS‑DES capability offset at runtime instead of using per‑controller hard‑coded offsets, updating all accesses accordingly.

Adds be_pause counter and fe_pause flag to correctly transition backend (BE) state to PAUSE instead of STOP when all front‑end streams are paused, fixing incorrect PAUSE_RELEASE handling and improving resource management.

Adds an optional kernel configuration to track and record each module that taints the kernel when it is unloaded, storing name, taint bits, and unload count, and prints this information alongside loaded modules.
Adds a lockdown check to the /proc/powerpc/ofdt write path, preventing untrusted device‑tree modifications when the kernel is in lockdown mode.

Adds .legacy_dai_naming = 1 to two ADI ASoC component driver structs, switching from the previous opt‑in non‑legacy naming flag to the new opt‑out legacy flag, aligning drivers with the updated naming scheme.
Switches allocation of an array of 4 ptp_pin_desc structures from kzalloc to kcalloc, adding overflow protection and using the semantically correct API.
The patch removes the redundant regs pointer from coredump_params, deletes the struct field, and updates ELF core dump code to use task_pt_regs(current) directly, simplifying core dump handling.
The commit adds a dma_release_channel() call in emac_probe() to clean up a DMA channel when probe fails, fixing a resource‑leak error handling path.

The patch modifies several Btrfs ioctl helper functions to take a struct inode * directly instead of a struct file *, removing redundant file_inode() calls. Callers in btrfs_ioctl and send code are updated to pass the existing inode, improving code reuse and clarity.

The patch updates the i2c‑scmi driver to use device_get_match_data() instead of a manual loop over ACPI IDs, and changes the methods pointer to const, simplifying acpi_smbus_cmi_add() and improving code clarity.

Adds a helper rdev_mdlock_deref that wraps rcu_dereference_protected with a lockdep check, replaces direct dereferences in raid5 code, and adds lock assertions, to correctly annotate accesses protected by mddev_lock and silence sparse warnings.

Implements kernel‑side handling of GTP Echo Request/Response for GTPv0 and GTPv1-U, adding restart counter support and netlink attributes, so devices created without a userspace daemon comply with the GTP specification.
Adds a safe macro bt_dev_name to handle NULL hdev and updates Bluetooth logging macros to use it, preventing null‑pointer dereference when printing device name.
Replaces cpumask_next* calls with cpumask_first* where start is -1, adds cpumask_first_zero helper, and updates several drivers and core files accordingly, improving code clarity and efficiency.

The commit adds a BROKEN dependency to the CLEVO_MAIL LED driver in Kconfig, marking it as broken until the interface issue (using brightness to set blink rate) is fixed, and updates the help text wording.
The patch modifies nl80211_associate to set the BSS pointer to NULL when the lookup returns an error, preventing later code from attempting to free an error pointer.

The commit corrects the Aquantia PHY driver to stop advertising 2.5 Gbps and 5 Gbps modes when the interface is limited to ≤1 Gbps. It adds bit definitions and updates aqr_config_aneg to set those bits only if the corresponding ethtool advertising bits are requested.
Adds missing RCU read lock and reference handling in bond_ethtool_get_ts_info, fixing a race when the function is invoked via setsockopt, as reported by syzbot.
Adds detailed logging of codec quirks (SSP, DMIC, GPIO) in the sof_es8336 driver, exposing the full quirk mask and conditional messages.
The commit renames the misspelled variables maxpctksize and maxpcktsize to the correct wMaxPacketSize in USB gadget UAC2 code, updating only debug/warn messages.
Adds code to include tracepoint probe fields when converting perf data to JSON by iterating over event fields and printing each name/value pair.
Corrects two typographical errors in kernel log messages: 'algorithm' and 'secret' in NVMe authentication code.
Corrects a duplicated word in a comment of amdgpu_fence.c and removes an extra 'the' in atombios.h documentation, improving comment clarity.

Refactors conv_uni_to_pc in consolemap.c to improve readability by extracting the pointer, adding explicit null checks, splitting a large conditional into smaller ones, and removing an unnecessary newline.
Adds a new MAINTAINERS entry for the Allwinner A31 MIPI CSI-2 bridge driver, listing maintainer, mailing list, and source file locations.
Adds device‑specific entries for two Chicony EasyCamera USB webcams, assigning a power‑line‑control‑limited quirk to work around their incorrect implementation.

The patch removes the obsolete odm_2to1_policy_applied flag and its checks, fixing a false detection of ODM combine mode changes that caused unnecessary stream reprogramming and intermittent black screens on HDMI.

The commit removes the unit address suffix from the panel endpoint nodes in the am335x device tree files, changing `endpoint@0` to `endpoint`. This corrects the DTS so the endpoint no longer requires a `reg` property, fixing a validation error.
Replace drm_mode_copy with drm_mode_init for on‑stack drm_mode structures, ensuring the list head is cleared and no leftover stack data remains.

The patch replaces a direct uncore register read-modify-write call with the intel_de_rmw accessor in the display power initialization, ensuring display code uses the proper DE register interface instead of low‑level uncore access.
Adds bounds checking for VCN and SDMA instance counts during AMDGPU discovery, ensuring they do not exceed driver-defined maximums and emitting an error if firmware reports too many instances.
Adds early sorting of the amode31 exception table and removes the later sorting, ensuring the table is ready before the early program check handler runs.

The commit removes the xpad driver's reset_resume callback, allowing the USB core to rebind the wireless controller after suspend/resume. This stops a hung URB that broke LED control and force‑feedback, restoring correct behavior on resume.
Changes fb_modesetting_disabled in fb.h to a static inline function, eliminating multiple definition linker errors when the header is included in multiple source files.

Adds Clause‑45 MDIO support to the lan743x Ethernet driver by defining MMD access constants, implementing helper functions for Clause‑45 reads/writes, and configuring the mii_bus to use C45 operations, along with related register definitions.
Adds a new stub header tools/include/linux/pfn.h defining PFN macros needed by test code.

The patch stops calling acpi_video_set_dmi_backlight_type() in the Toshiba ACPI driver and adds DMI entries in video_detect.c to force the vendor backlight driver for two Toshiba models, eliminating a race where the acpi_video0 device briefly appears then disappears.

The patch removes the driver’s attempt to read TIM information via the "dtim_assoc" IOVAR after a roam. Firmware no longer supports this call, causing repeated error logs. By eliminating the query, the driver stops generating the failure messages.
Replaces BUG_ON checks in do_notify_parent with WARN_ON_ONCE, so the kernel logs unexpected conditions instead of panicking, making debugging easier and avoiding crashes while holding core locks.
The patch deletes three redundant boolean initializations (bPacketMatchBSSID, bPacketToSelf, bPacketBeacon) from update_recvframe_phyinfo_88e, as they are overwritten later before use.
The patch rewrites shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp() to obtain a folio via shmem_get_folio_gfp(), unlock the folio, and derive the page, removing extra compound_head() calls and simplifying the code.

Adds validation for the NTFS boot sector's sectors_per_clusters field. Modifies true_sectors_per_clst to reject out‑of‑range values with -EINVAL and makes initialization abort on such errors, preventing a UBSAN shift‑out‑of‑bounds.
Fixes early KASAN initialization on RISC‑V when Sparsemem without vmemmap is enabled; replaces virt_to_page with pfn_pte to avoid null mem_section dereference.

The patch makes the DPAA2 Ethernet driver reuse scatter‑gather tables via a per‑CPU cache instead of allocating and freeing them for each nonlinear skb, enlarges the cache buffer size, and adds a macro defining the maximum entries.
Updates the dt-bindings maintainer entry in the MAINTAINERS file, replacing the old canonical.com email with the kernel.org address.
Adds a 'skip' enum value to the qcom,gsi-loader property in the device‑tree binding, documenting that GSI firmware loading can be omitted.

The commit modifies the SDM630 device tree: replaces a syscon node for the TCSR mutex with a direct hwlock node using the qcom,tcsr-mutex compatible, adds required #hwlock-cells, and removes the old hwlock wrapper, fixing DT schema validation errors.

Fixes a bug where returning from an interrupt to a soft‑masked (irqs‑disabled) context could lose a pending soft‑masked IRQ because the code incorrectly branched to the hard‑mask clearing path; adds proper branch and comment, and ensures the HARD_DIS flag is cleared correctly.
Adds an io_master helper, removes duplicate code, and changes topology initialization to mark IO master CPUs as non‑hotpluggable, preventing creation of their sysfs online control files.
Removes an unused variable 'last' and its associated dead code from remove_siblinginfo() in the IA-64 SMP boot code, simplifying the function without altering behavior.
Adjusts the selftest Makefile to correctly list compiled FP test programs under TEST_GEN_PROGS_EXTENDED and keep script tests under TEST_PROGS_EXTENDED, fixing the build behavior.
Adds rollback handling in fbcon_do_set_font: stores old font data, dimensions, and userfont flag, and restores them if vc_resize fails, fixing the inconsistent console state reported by syzbot.
Adds a 'power-domains' property to the MediaTek vcodec encoder device tree binding documentation, indicating the encoder may depend on a power domain.
Adds a range of power/thermal events to is_info_event so they are logged at INFO level, reflecting that they are purely informational and not errors.
Updates a devicetree binding YAML file, changing a $ref from a relative '../../leds/common.yaml#' to an absolute '/schemas/leds/common.yaml#' to follow preferred absolute path usage.
Adds EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL for mt6358 driver functions that were previously not exported, fixing undefined symbol errors when the driver is built as a module.
Reorders a bitfield in dp_128b_132b_supported_lttpr_link_rates struct to follow the DP2.0 specification, moving UHBR13_5 after UHBR20.
Adds an early‑return in slim_rx_mux_put when the requested mux value is already set, stopping an unnecessary change notification that caused spurious events.

The patch corrects concurrency handling in the FireWire core by acquiring card->lock before accessing card->local_node and bm_retries in fw_core_handle_bus_reset, moves lock acquisition out of fw_destroy_nodes, adds locking around its call in fw_core_remove_card, and documents the required lock.

The commit abstracts the policy‑setting routine into a chip‑specific operation, adds new policy enum values for RTL8852C, introduces wrapper functions, updates chip_ops and driver files to use the new callbacks, enabling additional hardware‑specific features.
The commit deletes a dead store to variable 'negative' in the AD2S1210 driver, eliminating an assignment that is never read and fixing a clang static analysis warning.

The patch modifies otx2_pf.c so that the PF driver forwards AF reply messages (including error codes) directly to the VF, instead of filtering them and sending an invalid message, preserving error information for the VF.
The patch removes a conditional that rejected devices with CHIP_IP_DISCOVERY flag, because IP‑based discovery support is now present, allowing the driver to load for those ASICs.

The patch modifies the Synopsys DesignWare HDMI driver to conditionally disable automatic General Control Packet (GCP) transmission when using standard 24‑bit color on sinks that lack Deep Color support, aligning the driver with HDMI 1.4b §6.5.3.

The patch modifies ARM IRQ entry/exit assembly to stop using register R9 (used for the task pointer) and instead uses R7/R8 to save FP and SP, ensuring R9 remains untouched between IRQ entry and exit.
Adds support for VSC info packet revision 4 required by PSR‑SU per eDP 1.5 spec, selecting rev4 when PSR version is SU_1 and populating the secondary‑data packet fields; retains rev2 handling.
The commit updates tools/tracing/Makefile to include rtla in the default build, install and clean targets, adding explicit rtla, rtla_install and rtla_clean rules and updating .PHONY.
The commit adds support for the PCA85073A RTC, which shares the PCF85063A programming model, by inserting a new I2C device ID and an OF compatible string into the driver.

The patch changes the registration of a USB Power Delivery (PD) partner object to use typec_partner_usb_power_delivery_register, passing the Type‑C partner as the parent, ensuring the PD object is correctly linked in the device hierarchy.

Adds MMIO‑based MDIO‑mux nodes and related Ethernet PHY definitions to the ls1043a‑qds device tree, updates aliases, makes the FPGA node compatible with simple‑mfd, and connects Ethernet interfaces to the new PHY nodes, enabling support for the board’s MDIO multiplexing hardware.
Moves the VHT antenna pattern capability bits from the generic VHT capability init to the stream init function, ensuring the 6 GHz band reports correct antenna configuration.
The commit fixes a bug where convert_context() could sleep while holding a spin lock by adding a gfp_t argument and passing GFP_ATOMIC in atomic contexts and GFP_KERNEL elsewhere.
Adds a platform driver shutdown callback for the ath11k WCN6750 device to stop DMA before the SMMU driver shuts down, preventing SMMU faults during system shutdown.

The patch adds a check in ocelot_port_bridge_flags to treat the NPI port as the physical port that maps to the CPU module, enabling the Felix DSA driver to control flooding via bridge port flags on the NPI port.

Updates the Qualcomm remoteproc device-tree binding documentation to include the qcom,msm8974-mss-pil compatible string, adds the optional mss-supply property with conditional requirement, and removes obsolete references from the q6v5.txt file.
Adds a null check for the DDC service in dc_submit_i2c_oem; if ddc is NULL the function now returns false instead of dereferencing a null pointer.
Removes the fsl,imx8qm-lpuart entry from the compatible enum in the fsl-lpuart devicetree binding YAML, because i.MX8QM is compatible with i.MX8QXP, forcing device tree nodes to list both strings.

The patch moves the removal of a context from the i915->gem.contexts list from context_close() to the release_work after the final reference is dropped, protecting list traversal used by i915_perf and fixing a GPF caused by a dangling link.
Adds a helper to allocate MSI‑X vectors for all virtqueues and the config interrupt, integrates it into the IRQ request path, and logs when fewer vectors are obtained.
Removes snd_BUG() from snd_usbmidi_output_open; when a NULL port is found (invalid endpoint), the driver now returns -ENXIO instead of triggering a BUG, avoiding spurious kernel oops.

The patch changes sony_nc_kbd_backlight_setup to call the SNC probe only when a separate probe_base address is present. For the 0x153 backlight handle, probing without a distinct address previously acted as a set‑to‑0 operation, unintentionally turning off the keyboard backlight. The added check skips the probe, preserving backlight state.
Restricts linebuffer pixel depth to 36 bpp only on DCN display engines, using 30 bpp for DCE versions to avoid dithering bugs observed on DCE‑11.2 and earlier hardware.
Renames the local variable 'rate' to 'tx_rate' in ieee80211_calc_expected_tx_airtime to avoid shadowing the outer 'rate' variable, enhancing code clarity.
Wraps address casts in x86 boot code with absolute_pointer() to silence GCC -Warray-bounds warnings, updating inline assembly operands accordingly.
Adds GPIO button and LED definitions for Asus RTN-10U board and registers them, enabling kernel support for its buttons and LEDs.

The patch removes the mutable irq_chip field from owl_pinctrl, defines a const irq_chip with IRQCHIP_IMMUTABLE flag, and uses gpio_irq_chip_set_chip; it also updates IRQ handling code to use irqd_to_hwirq and helper functions.

The commit updates the imx8mp-phycore-som device tree: it disables boot‑on/always‑on for LDO4 (not connected) and enables those flags for LDO5 (required for SD‑Card VSEL), correcting the regulator configuration.
The patch replaces direct clock enable/disable calls with mchp_pit64b_suspend/resume, adds a resume call at init, and simplifies error handling in the PIT64B timer driver.

The patch normalises how underscores are inserted into firmware file‑name macros for Intel UC (GUC/HUC) firmware, moving the delimiter handling into the generic concatenation macros so that all paths are built uniformly.

The patch fixes a resource‑leak bug in the SonicVibes ALSA PCI driver: when the probe function fails, the driver previously omitted snd_card_free(), causing improper cleanup. It adds an internal __snd_sonic_probe and wraps it with snd_card_free_on_error to ensure correct release order.

The commit introduces support for the Apple Audio DMA Controller (ADMAC) on Apple Silicon SoCs. It adds a Kconfig option, updates the DMA Makefile, and provides a full driver implementation handling channel allocation, descriptor management, interrupt handling, and DMA engine integration.

The patch changes udl_handle_damage to take a const struct drm_rect * instead of separate x, y, width, height arguments, updates callers to build and pass a drm_rect, and adjusts internal field accesses, simplifying the code.
Adds extensive BPF selftest cases for btf_dump, introducing new structs and expected output to verify correct handling of padding and packing edge cases.
Adds a call to unregister_candev() in the probe error path so that if GPIO setup fails the CAN device is properly unregistered, fixing a resource‑cleanup bug.
Adjusts indentation of a bullet list in Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-class-thermal to satisfy the documentation build warning about missing blank line after a list.
Adds USB_1 over‑current detection to the Verdin imx8mp board by configuring the USB controller node, defining the over‑current pin, and removing the previous generic GPIO mapping.
Adds definitions, structs, and handling code for the CMD_ERROR_EVENT command in the Kvaser USB leaf driver, integrating it into the command dispatch.
Renames ID_AA64ISAR2_EL1 field macros to include the _EL1 suffix and updates all references, aligning naming conventions without altering functionality.

The patch updates egress rate‑limiting code to handle CN10K hardware differences: adds CN10K burst limits, selects limits based on device, changes maxrate to u64, and builds the correct register value for both device families.
The patch replaces a BUG_ON in efx_unregister_netdev with a WARN_ON that logs a warning and returns, adding recovery logic to avoid a kernel panic when netdev_priv does not match the efx struct.
The commit changes the uid_strings array from a function‑local const to a static const, removing its stack allocation and slightly reducing object size.
The commit removes the never‑used UsbTxAggDescNum field from hal_data_8188e, introduces a constant USB_TXAGG_DESC_NUM with value 0x6, and updates all references to use the constant.
The commit updates the uml_vector_default_bpf function signature and its declaration to take a const void *mac instead of void *mac, aligning with recent constification of MAC address handling.
The patch reworks how testmode antenna masks are handled for MT7915, treating them as antenna_mask instead of chainmask, removing unnecessary shifts and simplifying condition checks.

The patch zeroes the page->private field when a new page is allocated for migration and when a tail page is created during huge page splitting, fixing mismatches that caused bugs like ceph's PG_private check.
Corrects a misspelled word in a comment in acp-pdm.c; the change only touches documentation, not code execution.
Adds missing register and bitfield definitions for the Mediatek Ethernet PCS, updating the header with correct masks and constants based on recent hardware investigation.

The patch updates the fbdev hot‑unplug workaround to emit a warning when a framebuffer lacks an associated device, and rewrites the surrounding comment. It keeps the existing unregister behavior but adds diagnostic output.

The patch removes per-zone capacity array from F2FS, adds a single unusable_blocks_per_sec field, updates calculations to use this uniform capacity, and adds a check that aborts mounting if zones have differing capacities, simplifying zone handling.
Updates a documentation file to replace the GPLv2 boilerplate with an SPDX‑License‑Identifier line, removing the old license notice.
The commit deletes an unused extern declaration of sni_cpu_time_init() from the MIPS sni.h header, as the function was removed earlier.
Moves the compbuf size programming before clock updates in dcn20_optimize_bandwidth to avoid P-State hangs caused by the previous ordering.

Adds a pinctrl controller node to the MT6795 device tree, with compatible string, register definitions, interrupt specs, GPIO and interrupt controller properties, and includes the pinfunc binding header.
Corrects numerous typographical errors in comments, strings, and documentation across the ath10k driver files.
The commit simplifies the c67x00 driver remove routine by deleting unnecessary NULL checks before freeing IRQ and releasing memory, relying on the guarantee that resources were obtained during probe.
The commit updates the KVM documentation to clarify MSR filtering semantics, correct terminology, fix an off‑by‑one description error, and remove redundant sections. No code behavior is changed.
Renames page_swap_flags to folio_swap_flags and updates its usage to operate on folio structures, moving the page‑to‑folio conversion down a level.
The commit updates warning strings in mlx5e_rss_warn, replacing 'LRO state' with 'packet merge state' to reflect a naming change; no functional code is altered.

Implements nested VMLOAD/VMSAVE support in AMD SVM KVM. Introduces a flag for virtual VMLOAD/VMSAVE enablement, conditional intercept logic, updates CPUID handling, sets CPU capability bits, and restores NPT detection helper.

The patch changes cdns_fill_msg_resp to only copy response data into msg->buf for READ messages, leaving the buffer untouched for WRITE commands, preventing unintended modification of the caller's buffer.

Introduces a local variable `dev` for `&pdev->dev` and replaces all direct uses of `&pdev->dev` with this variable across ACPI, devm allocations, regmap, IRQ chip, and MFD registration, making the driver code cleaner without functional changes.

The patch introduces a struct to hold temporary variables used by dml32_CalculateSwathAndDETConfiguration, adds it to the dummy_vars container, changes the function signature to accept a pointer, and updates all call sites and internal references to use the struct fields, thereby reducing stack consumption.

The commit updates the Chinese translation of the admin‑guide index, reformatting the 'Todolist' sections from plain indented lines to proper bullet lists using asterisks, improving readability of the generated HTML documentation.
Moves the SVM TSC ratio constant definitions from svm.c into the public header svm.h, aligning the code with the SVM specification and centralizing these macros.
Adds a new enum value to the Renesas USB2 PHY devicetree binding YAML to document the RZ/G2UL SoC, noting it uses the existing compatible string as fallback.

The patch rewrites the LTC2983 IIO driver to use the generic device‑property (fwnode) API instead of OF‑specific calls, making it work on non‑device‑tree platforms and adjusting memory allocation and endian handling accordingly.
Adds alternate pinmux definitions for DCMI pins (dcmi_pins_c and dcmi_sleep_pins_c) in the STM32MP15 pinctrl device tree to support the AV96 board.

The commit reverts a prior change that altered sbitmap_queue_wake_up to accept a count argument. It restores the original function signature and call sites, removing the count parameter, because the change caused CPU stalls and possible infinite loops.
The patch deletes the unused qid member from struct mt76_queue and removes all assignments to it in TX and MCU queue initialization for SDIO, USB, and generic code, as it is no longer referenced.
Reorders operations in moxart_remove() so that register writes occur before mmc_free_host(), preventing use‑after‑free of the host structure.
The patch adds a line that sets the sta.mlo flag based on the link_id when preparing a new station, ensuring the flag reflects whether the connection uses Multi‑Link Operation.

Adds minimal user_regset support for the m68k architecture, enabling core dump handling in the ELF FDPIC loader. Includes header includes, a get function, regset definitions, and a view returned by task_user_regset_view, compiled only when CONFIG_BINFMT_ELF_FDPIC and CONFIG_ELF_CORE are enabled.
The commit adds the V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_MODIFY_LAYOUT flag to the HFLIP and VFLIP controls in the imx319 driver so that the V4L2 core knows the image layout changes when flips are applied.
The patch changes process_msg_close from returning int to void because it always returns 0, and updates its call site accordingly, removing the unused return value.
Implements the SBI v0.3 System Reset (SRST) extension for RISC‑V KVM guests by adding the extension struct and handler, enabling poweroff and reboot calls from the guest.
Adds optional 16‑byte NOP padding before each x86 function via new Kconfig options, compiler flags, and assembly macros, enabling software call‑stack tracking and kCFI/FineIBT support.

The patch renames all occurrences of "video_pll1" to "video_pll" in the i.MX8MN clock driver and its DT binding header, matching the reference manual. Old symbols are kept as aliases for backward compatibility. No functional behavior is altered.

The patch refactors i9xx_update_wm() to use the existing single_enabled_crtc() helper instead of a custom 'enabled' variable, removing the ad‑hoc tracking variable and simplifying the logic for legacy watermarks.

Adds checks when entering MALL static screen to ensure PSR panels are already in PSR and avoids overriding link settings for phantom streams, fixing incorrect handling of PSR panels during MALL entry.
Changes audit_init_parent to accept a const struct path, preventing modification of the path argument and improving const-correctness.
The commit modifies the TAS2770 codec driver to set the minimum channel count from 2 to 1, enabling mono playback streams for the mono speaker amp that can downmix and switch channels.
Replace pm_runtime_get_sync with pm_runtime_resume_and_get in the stm32 vrefbuf regulator driver, removing extra error handling and simplifying power‑management calls.

The patch modifies the Intel raw NAND controller probe to read the chip‑select ('reg') from the NAND chip's child OF node and passes that node to nand_set_flash_node, correcting the previous use of the controller node.

The commit replaces XFS inode fork size macros with inline type‑checked helper functions, adds those functions to xfs_inode.h, and updates all call sites across the XFS codebase to use the new functions.
The patch corrects hci_read_buffer_size_sync to stop using the LE‑only command HCI_OP_LE_READ_BUFFER_SIZE_V2 and moves that logic to hci_le_read_buffer_size_sync, fixing incorrect command usage.
The patch replaces a fixed-size stack array for the efuse buffer with a kmalloc‑allocated buffer and frees it before returning, removing the __aligned(4) qualifier.
The commit changes several functions in dcn32_hubbub.c from external linkage to static because they are only used within that file, eliminating compiler warnings about missing prototypes.

The commit fixes a crash in the ptp_ocp driver where sysfs_remove_group was called on attribute groups that were never created. It computes the groups to register based on firmware capabilities, registers them with sysfs_create_groups, and removes them with sysfs_remove_groups, adding proper error handling.
Removes the declaration of the unused function intel_gt_create_kobj from intel_gt_sysfs.h, cleaning up the header and eliminating dead code.
Changes Kconfig for MAX9759 codec: replaces 'select GPIOLIB' with 'depends on GPIOLIB' to avoid forcing the GPIO library when not needed, eliminating build warnings.
Introduces folio_batch_move_lru and related helpers, replacing pagevec‑based LRU handling with folio_batch infrastructure in mm/swap.c, updating rotate and drain code accordingly.
Removes the unnecessary f2fs_lock_op/f2fs_unlock_op around f2fs_alloc_nid in f2fs_new_inode because allocation does not need checkpoint blocking and the nat_tree_lock already protects the operation.
Adds a new function perf_cpu_map__is_subset to the perf cpumap library and its header, enabling callers to test whether one CPU map is a subset of another.

The patch adds explicit include directives for seq_file.h, pinctrl/consumer.h, pinconf-generic.h and reorders all headers alphabetically, removing duplicated generic includes in the Lynxpoint pinctrl driver.

Removes the redundant tcf_connmark_walker and tcf_connmark_search functions and their registrations in act_connmark_ops, relying on the generic walker/search implementations, thus simplifying the connmark action code.

Adds support for 64‑bit software bundle initialization in the Nouveau GPU driver by introducing sw_bundle64_init handling, sending high 32 bits when needed, and updating related structures and cleanup.

The patch replaces the old vb2_find_timestamp + index lookup pattern with the new vb2_find_buffer API, changing stored reference buffers from indices to direct vb2_buffer pointers and simplifying related helper functions.

Adds a suite of KUnit tests for MCTP route input key and tag matching, introducing a helper macro, a test parameter struct, a test function exercising various key configurations, and registers the new test case.

The patch updates the cs46xx ALSA driver probe routine to route all error paths to a new label that calls snd_card_free(card) before returning, ensuring proper cleanup of allocated resources that were previously left unreleased on probe failures.
Switches error handling in the mxsfb DRM driver to use the dev_err_probe() helper, removing manual dev_err checks and adding a deferred‑probe hint in debugfs.

The patch replaces all uses of page->freelist with page->index in bootmem handling, because freelist is meant for slab. Using the integer index avoids pointer casts and aligns with the intended field usage.

Switches the sdw-mockup driver to use the new snd_sdw_params_to_config helper for converting PCM hw_params to SoundWire stream and port configuration, adding the appropriate header and simplifying the code.
Fixes a memory leak in configfs_create_dir and configfs_create_link by adding missing configfs_put calls on error paths to correct reference counting.

The commit refactors error handling in XDP redirect code, changing returned errno values to distinguish allocation failures (ENOMEM) from full Rx buffers (ENOBUFS), enabling drivers to react appropriately.

The patch removes the code that unbinds the NVMe driver when a controller reset fails and instead shuts the controller down, marks namespaces dead, and sets the controller state to DEAD, keeping the driver bound.
Adds `additionalProperties: false` to OPP binding schemas to ensure only documented properties are allowed, tightening the device‑tree documentation.
Adds a missing free_uid() call in __io_sqe_files_scm() to release the UID reference when no files are processed, preventing a memory leak.
Adds select statements for CRYPTO_AES and CRYPTO_CBC in the ARM NEON AES‑BS config so the algorithm has required generic fallbacks, preventing registration failure at boot.

The patch changes the soc_setup_card_name macro to accept the card struct, adds a length check for the driver name, and logs an error when the name exceeds the driver field size, improving driver name handling in ASoC.
Adds a new board configuration (adl_rt5682) for Intel SOF platforms to support the alc5682 codec without a speaker amplifier, and registers it in the ACPI machine match table.
The commit removes the unused gfp_flags argument from null_alloc_page, hard‑codes GFP_NOIO inside the function, and updates its sole caller, simplifying the null_blk driver code.

Adds a configurable sysfs interface for DAMON, introducing Kconfig option, Makefile entry, and a large sysfs implementation that creates hierarchical directories and files for configuring DAMON contexts, targets, intervals, etc.
Adds a missing NET dependency to INTEL_HFI_THERMAL in Kconfig, resolving a warning and numerous build errors caused by an unmet direct dependency.
Corrects swapped bitmask definitions in Mediatek Ethernet driver macros so that RX_DMA_GET_SPORT extracts 3 bits and RX_DMA_GET_SPORT_V2 extracts 4 bits, fixing incorrect source‑port decoding.

The commit resets two local boolean flags at the start of a prefetch calculation loop in the AMD DC DML code, fixing a bug where the loop failed to exit properly after a failure, causing excessive use of VStartup lines.

Adds mutex locking around the circular buffer updates in roccat_report_event to synchronize with roccat_read, eliminating a race where the buffer could be freed while being copied to userspace, thus fixing a use‑after‑free bug.
The commit removes many #if CONFIG_DRM_AMD_DC_DCN guards in the amdgpu_dm driver, making code unconditional because the DC layer is OS‑agnostic. This cleans up redundant compile‑time configuration.
Ensures the DTIM period set for a link is retained and correctly propagated, removing code that cleared it and adding proper handling after beacon processing.

Adds a list_for_each_table_entry macro to iterate over ctl_table entries until procname is NULL and replaces existing manual loops with this macro throughout proc_sysctl.c, improving readability and reducing duplication.
Adjusts io_uring multishot accept handling to correctly drop the operation when posting an auxiliary CQE fails, fixing the ordering and return logic for overflow cases.

The commit fixes incorrect speed initialization for CPU/DSA ports in the mv88e6xxx DSA driver by fetching MAC capabilities via mv88e6xxx_get_caps() before using them, correcting the default 10M speed caused by missing capabilities.
The commit updates ath10k driver code to satisfy recent checkpatch warnings by replacing strlcpy with strscpy and correcting a printf format specifier, without altering runtime behavior.
Adds the "#sound-dai-cells" property to the it66121 device‑tree binding to document audio support.
Adds a guard in io_sendmsg_zc to reject zero‑copy sendmsg on sockets lacking the SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC flag, returning -EOPNOTSUPP.

Adds ethtool --identify support to the Netronome NFP driver by implementing a phys_id handler that toggles the NIC's panel LED via a new firmware command, and exposing it through the driver’s ethtool operations.
Adds a YAML device‑tree binding file for the Himax hx83112b touchscreen controller and registers it in MAINTAINERS, enabling kernel to recognize and configure this hardware.
Adds a fixed regulator, enables the second PCIe controller and its combphy, and defines pinctrl for PCIe enable and reset in the quartz64-b device tree, providing hardware support for PCIe 2.

The patch separates nvme_kill_queues into two parts: nvme_mark_namespaces_dead (marks all namespace disks dead) and moves the unquiescing of I/O queues to callers, updating all call sites and renaming the function.

The patch removes all checks for the CE (correctable error) status in various UMC RAS error‑address query functions, leaving only the UE (uncorrectable error) condition and cleaning related comments. This simplifies the code because only UE errors are currently handled.

The commit resolves sparse static analysis warnings in PowerPC time code by declaring missing symbols, adding the proper header for rtc_lock, moving dtl_consumer definition after its header, and removing a duplicate extern declaration.
Adds <linux/string_helpers.h> and replaces an inline conditional string with the str_enable_disable() helper in a dev_dbg call, improving readability without changing runtime behavior.
Adds conditional loading of xeCJK.sty in the documentation preamble, preventing LaTeX errors on systems where texlive-xecjk is absent.

The patch replaces struct sockaddr with struct sockaddr_storage in NFS code, updates related function signatures and casts, and adjusts memcpy calls to use the full address size, removing fortify overflow warnings and correcting potential buffer overflows.
The patch updates btrfs ordered-data.c to replace the macro INT_LIMIT(loff_t) with OFFSET_MAX, improving code readability without altering logic.

The patch removes the obsolete of_gpio.h header and replaces the driver’s use of the deprecated of_mm_gpio_chip and of_* helpers with the standard gpio_chip API, adding explicit ioremap for registers and using devm_gpiochip_add_data.
Ensures CU masking works correctly on GFX10+ GPUs with WGP mode by adjusting mask handling and adding validation, fixing incorrect dispatch behavior.
The patch replaces a custom stop_irq_work function and devm_add_action with the helper devm_delayed_work_autocancel, simplifying delayed‑work handling in the max14656 charger detector driver.
Adds a hardware capability flag for ARM64 MTE asymmetric mode (FEAT_MTE3), updating documentation, kernel and uapi headers, cpufeature table, and cpuinfo string so userspace can detect support.

The patch extracts all combo PHY register definitions from i915_reg.h into a new header intel_combo_phy_regs.h, updates driver source files to include this header, and removes the now‑redundant block from i915_reg.h. No functional changes, only code reorganization.

The commit refactors the palmas MFD driver probe function to obtain driver-specific data via device_get_match_data() instead of manually using of_match_device(), removing unused variables and simplifying code.

The patch replaces manual 32‑bit reads of high/low registers with the generic ioread64_hi_lo()/iowrite64_hi_lo() helpers, adding the appropriate header and simplifying timestamp extraction in the PCH PTP driver.
The commit deletes the Promise SATA SX8 block driver: removes its Kconfig option, Makefile entry, and the entire source file, as the hardware is obscure and unmaintained.
The commit updates the QCOM USB VBUS regulator device‑tree binding documentation, renaming the example node from dcdc@1100 to usb-vbus-regulator@1100 to use a more appropriate generic name.
Adds UNTRAIN_RET macro to Xen error entry so that Xen's entry path includes the speculation‑mitigation return‑training instruction, ensuring the same protection as other entry points.
The patch deletes the legacy <linux/gpio.h> header from drivers/media/i2c/ccs/ccs-core.c because the driver already includes <linux/gpio/consumer.h>, making the former include unnecessary.
The commit adds linux/cyclades.h to the no-header-test list in usr/include/Makefile, so the kbuild header check no longer examines this file, which now emits a warning when included.

The commit adds a dma_dev pointer to mt76_dev, initializes it with the PCI device, and replaces all DMA mapping/unmapping calls to use this pointer, allowing the driver to override the device used for DMA. This enables WED support requiring non‑coherent DMA.
Renames btrfs_insert_file_extent to btrfs_insert_hole_extent, removes unused parameters, and updates all call sites so the function now only inserts holes with zeroed metadata fields.
The patch frees the debug_help_string buffer during module cleanup and after its use, eliminating a kmemleak reported when inserting and removing the orangefs module.

Rewrites the qcom,adsp devicetree binding YAML to replace maxItems constraints with explicit interrupt and interrupt-name item lists and adjusts conditional schema, simplifying handling of an optional last interrupt.
The commit raises the GT reset watchdog timeout from 5 seconds to 60 seconds, giving resets more time before the driver wedges the device and discarding user work.

Adds PTP interrupt support to the sparx5 Ethernet driver: introduces ptp_irq field, requests the IRQ, implements a threaded handler that processes two‑step timestamps, matches them to skbs, and records hardware timestamps.
Adds a requires_cpu flag to distinguish uncore events that need a specific CPU, replaces misuse of system_wide flag, updates struct and logic in perf to handle this correctly.
Adds kernel-doc comments for two new fields in struct tegra_pmc to describe their purpose, without changing code behavior.
Adds a null‑pointer check after calling platform_get_resource() in the mt6397 RTC driver; if the call returns NULL the probe returns -EINVAL, preventing a dereference of a NULL pointer.

The patch renames the existing filter flow‑group identifiers to include “vlan”, updating macros, function names, variable names and struct fields in the Mellanox mlx5 bridge driver to distinguish them from the upcoming QinQ group, improving code readability.
The patch deletes the now‑unused declaration of arch_kprobe_override_function() from arch/x86/include/asm/kprobes.h, as the function itself was removed in a prior commit.
Moves the -mno-branch-likely flag check into Kconfig and adds it only when the compiler supports it, preventing clang warnings from becoming fatal errors and breaking builds.
Changes platform_get_irq_byname to use the generic fwnode_irq_get_byname API, allowing named IRQ lookup for both OF and ACPI described devices.

Adds hda_codec_device_remove() helper to encapsulate codec removal, updates the header, and replaces the direct snd_hdac_ext_bus_device_remove call in hda.c with this helper, improving separation between controller and codec code.

The patch adds two new header files (`mmhub_3_0_1_offset.h` and `mmhub_3_0_1_sh_mask.h`) that define a comprehensive set of register offsets and bit‑field masks for the MMHUB block of AMD GPUs, specifically for version 3.0.1. No functional code changes are made; the commit simply expands the register database to support newer hardware revisions.
The patch replaces three sprintf calls with snprintf in ptp_ocp_verify, supplying the buffer size to avoid possible overflow and make the code easier to review.
The patch rewrites devm_clk_hw_register_clkdev() to use devm_add_action_or_reset() instead of manual devres_alloc()/devres_add(), removing extra code while keeping behavior unchanged.
Adds missing bounds checks for timestamp and command‑queue counter offsets in habanalabs driver, changing a > comparison to >= and validating cq offset against buffer size.
The commit corrects the dev_warn format string for an unsigned 32‑bit variable, changing %d to %#x and consolidating the call into a single line.

Extends the Sparx5 driver to support additional TC flower match keys (IPv4/IPv6 addresses, control flags, ports, basic protocol info, VLAN, TCP flags, IP TOS) for the IS2 VCAP and adds a 128‑bit keyfield API for IPv6 addresses with corresponding parsing handlers.

Adds support for Amlogic Meson S4 SoCs in the meson‑gpio IRQ driver by defining a new register, implementing an S4‑specific irq_set_type function, creating a parameter struct for 12‑line GPIO IRQs, and registering the compatible string in the device match table.
The commit introduces a new CPU feature flag X86_FEATURE_PERFMON_V2 for AMD processors, mapping CPUID leaf 0x80000022 bit 0 to this flag and updating the scattered feature table accordingly.
Fixes a 32‑byte memory leak in ibmvnic reset handling by freeing the temporary rwi structure when the last reset succeeds, correcting logic introduced by a previous commit.
The patch casts __fls to unsigned long in a dev_err call to silence a %ld format warning on arc, m68k and sparc, enabling successful allmodconfig builds on those architectures.

The commit renames the driver file ice_sriov.c and its header to ice_vf_mbx.c, updates the Makefile and include directives, and prepares the code for future Scalable IOV support while keeping existing SR-IOV logic unchanged.

The patch corrects FS_CP_DATA_IO accounting in f2fs when data_flush is enabled by separating cp_task into cp_task (for checkpoint accounting) and wb_task (to avoid deadlock), adding a new field and adjusting related functions.

Adds a guard in ieee80211_tx_control_port() to avoid calling __ieee80211_select_queue() when the hardware has fewer than four TX queues, fixing a regression that caused invalid queue selection on non‑QoS drivers such as ralink rt2500‑pci.

Adds support for NVIDIA Tegra234 Multi‑Gigabit Ethernet (MGBE) by creating a Kconfig option, Makefile entry, and a new dwmac‑tegra.c driver implementing probe, suspend/resume, serdes handling and integration with the stmmac framework.
Adds string representations for two iavf driver states (__IAVF_INIT_EXTENDED_CAPS and __IAVF_INIT_CONFIG_ADAPTER) in iavf_state_str, fixing missing debug prints of state transitions.
Adds support in perf inject to copy the kcore_dir from the input perf.data to the output, introducing a flag and copy routine to preserve kernel symbols and related files.
Adds a reference to the common CAN controller binding in the sun4i-a10 CAN device tree binding file, updating the YAML to include the shared can-controller.yaml schema.

Moves the Renesas product register devicetree binding file from Documentation/devicetree/bindings/soc to Documentation/devicetree/bindings/hwinfo, updates its $id URL and adds the new path to MAINTAINERS.
The patch removes redundant (u8) casts in two comparisons against VERSION_8190_BD, which is already an 8‑bit constant, simplifying the code without altering functionality.
The patch deletes an unnecessary #include <linux/msi.h> from drivers/iommu/of_iommu.c because the file does not use any symbols from that header. No other modifications are made.
Adds support for NAND devices with OOB size >1 KB by introducing new BCH geometry calculations that ensure the bad‑block mark stays in a data chunk, with a fallback to separate ECC for metadata.

Adds conditional compilation guards around Energy Model functions in the cppc_cpufreq driver so that when CONFIG_ENERGY_MODEL is disabled on arm64 the unused functions are omitted, eliminating -Werror=unused-function warnings and avoiding unnecessary work.
Initializes previously uninitialized variables and adds return‑value/pointer checks to silence smatch warnings, preventing use of undefined data and invalid dereferences.
The commit removes duplicated wake‑up interrupt definitions from the Exynos850 pin controller device‑tree node, correcting the DTS so that only the appropriate interrupt entries remain.
Adds interrupt configuration and handler callbacks to the KSZ9477 PHY driver, enabling interrupt support similar to other Micrel PHYs.

Adds support for the Apple DART2 IOMMU used in M1 Pro/Max/Ultra SoCs by introducing a new PTE format, address mask/shift, protection bits, and registering the new format in the io-pgtable infrastructure.
The patch updates scripts/checkpatch.pl to ignore macro definitions that start with "case", preventing the tool from flagging such macros as errors.

Replaces a manual size calculation in pwc_decompress with the struct_size() helper to correctly compute the allocation size, eliminating flexible‑array misuse and potential integer overflow, and silences a sparse warning.

The patch replaces nodes_weight() with nodes_empty() in x86 NUMA initialization and emulation code, because nodes_empty() can stop early when a set bit is found, making the check more efficient while preserving existing semantics.
Adds dma-channel-mask to Tegra GPCDMA DT nodes and updates interrupts list, correcting previous driver limitation of channels to 31 and aligning DT with hardware.

The patch changes the KVM_X86_OP macro to invoke WARN_ON when a required function pointer in kvm_x86_ops is NULL, using the corrected annotation system, thereby detecting missing implementations at module load time.

The patch removes the generic vm_xsave_req_perm call from kvm_util.c, adds a bit argument to the function, updates its declaration and implementation, and invokes it with the appropriate bit inside the amx_test self‑test, allowing other tests to request different xsave bits.

The commit updates the VC4 HDMI driver to correctly detect the hdmi_enable_4kp60 configuration flag. It replaces the previous clk_round_rate() check with rpi_firmware_clk_get_max_rate() to obtain the clock’s maximum rate, fixing broken detection after a clock subsystem rewrite.

Makes the 'chip' (and parent device) argument mandatory in hwmon registration APIs, updating documentation and adding NULL checks to enforce correct usage and stop developers from merely renaming the function without providing proper chip info.
Adds <linux/bits.h> and replaces all (1 << n) constants with BIT(n) in the lm90 hardware monitoring driver, improving readability without changing functionality.
Adds module_elf_check_arch to verify ELF ABI version for PowerPC64 modules, overriding generic check; ensures correct ABI level based on CONFIG_PPC64_ELF_ABI_V2.

The patch rewrites simpledrm to use the generic DRM atomic helper infrastructure (plane, crtc, encoder, connector) instead of the old simple‑KMS helpers, updating structures, init calls and helper functions without changing driver behavior.

The patch replaces manual delayed‑work init and explicit cancel in remove() with devm_delayed_work_autocancel, removing the unsafe cancel call on an uninitialized work struct and deleting the now‑unused remove() method.
Adds calls to devlink_port_type_clear in error paths and cleanup of mlx4 port initialization to undo a previous devlink_port_type_set, preventing stale port type state.
Implements a parallel JPEG decode worker for MT8195, adding hardware selection, workqueue handling, and driver structures to run up to three decode engines concurrently.

The patch updates the CDCE925 clock driver to use the new simple I2C probe API (probe_new) and i2c_match_id for driver data lookup, moving the device ID table earlier and removing the unused id argument.
Replaces a manual cancel_delayed_work_sync + devm_add_action pattern with the helper devm_delayed_work_autocancel, adding the appropriate header and removing custom cancel function.

The patch moves the keep‑to‑write handling from ext4_writepage into ext4_bio_write_page, ensuring that when some buffers cannot be written the TOWRITE tag remains set so concurrent WB_SYNC_ALL writeback does not skip the page, preventing data loss during transaction commit.

Moves snapshot lookup from devlink_nl_region_read_snapshot_fill to devlink_nl_cmd_region_read_dumpit, passes snapshot directly, removes unused attrs parameter, simplifying code and enabling earlier error return for invalid snapshot IDs.
The commit raises the sleep delay from 5 to 15 seconds in two SELinux deprecation paths (runtime disable and checkreqprot) to make the deprecation warnings more noticeable to users.
The patch updates the driver constant GS_MAX_INTF from 2 to 3 and adjusts the comment, enabling support for STM32G3 devices that have up to three CAN-FD channels.
The patch deletes the variable 'found_devs' and its increment statements from qla2xxx's local loop configuration function, as the variable was never used elsewhere.
Removes many VPRINTK debug prints and the ata_scsi_dump_cdb function from libata, as they are redundant with tracepoints, cleaning up the code.
Updates the kernel-doc comment for the vmbus driver registration function, correcting the documented name to match the actual prototype and remove a build warning.

The patch replaces the mandatory back_lock around iscsi_get_task/put_task with a lock‑free refcount check, adds iscsi_get_task returning bool, and updates callers to handle the case where the task is already being freed, improving performance and race safety.

The patch rewrites debug and error messages in drm_edid.c to use device‑specific macros (drm_dbg_kms, drm_err) and adds connector identifiers, also consolidates tile debug output into a single line. No functional logic is altered.

The patch extracts the post‑power‑up work (state read, BAR restore, ASPM reconfiguration) from pci_power_up into a new helper pci_set_full_power_state, adjusts pci_power_up to return a flag and set the state earlier, and updates callers accordingly.
Renames ICL-specific Thunderbolt AUX power domain enums to the spec-defined TBT1-4 names and updates related string tables and power‑domain mappings.

The patch deletes the remaining IDE‑related sections from Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst, renumbers subsequent sections, and updates a comment in drivers/block/pktcdvd.c to reference the correct SCSI driver path. It only touches documentation and comments, not kernel functionality.
The patch modifies amdgpu_display_framebuffer_init to also skip the tiling‑flag check when virtual display is enabled, preventing a GFX9+ warning that occurs with vkms lacking FB modifiers.

The patch changes ACPI_FLUSH_CPU_CACHE() to call wbinvd only when not running under a hypervisor, adding comments. This avoids executing WBINVD in virtual machines, which can cause a #VE exception on TDX guests.
The patch adds a WARN_ON_ONCE check and caps the returned byte count to prevent tcp_read_sock() from looping forever when recv_actor() returns a value larger than the buffer length.

The commit changes rhashtable's internal locking from bh‑safe (local_bh_disable/enable) to irq‑safe (local_irq_save/restore), returning flags and updating unlock calls, enabling the hash table to be used in interrupt contexts.
Adds an extra length check in vtpm_proxy_fops_read to ensure req_len does not exceed the internal buffer, silencing a GCC array‑bounds warning and making the code safer for future changes.

Switches the driver to use DEFINE_RUNTIME_DEV_PM_OPS and pm_ptr macros, removing __maybe_unused attributes so the dev_pm_ops structure and functions are omitted when CONFIG_PM is disabled, improving compile‑time handling.
Adds the correct <linux/kstrtox.h> include to several RTC driver files and sysfs.c because kstrto* functions were moved from kernel.h, ensuring the code compiles after the header relocation.

The patch changes sdma_v5_2_hw_fini to always disable the SDMA engine during hardware finalization and, if running under SR‑IOV, immediately re‑enable it and its context switch, clearing the DRM entity so the resume path works correctly.

Adds a delayed‑work timeout mechanism for the Mediatek JPEG decoder driver: new struct fields for timeout work and hardware parameters, a work handler that resets hardware and reports buffer errors, cancellation in IRQ, and initialization in probe.
Adds extended‑blank (extra vblank) support to allow zstate entry during FreeSync, introduces capability flags, debug option, new stream update fields, and programming of hardware registers.

Removes the &ipa_fw_mem reserved memory node from the sc7180‑trogdor device‑tree because the board does not use this carveout, which otherwise overlaps with another region and triggers an OVERLAP DETECTED boot message.
Refactors the merge_state function in Btrfs to use prev_state/next_state helpers instead of manual rb_prev/rb_next traversal, simplifying and cleaning up the code without changing behavior.
Updates the hqd_destroy callback prototype to use enum kfd_preempt_type instead of uint32_t, aligning with actual implementations and eliminating a CFI type mismatch on AMD GPUs.

The commit updates the Meson SM1 Odroid device tree, changing the tf_io regulator enable GPIO from active‑high to open‑drain. This corrects the regulator handling after a reboot, eliminating a boot loop.
